answer: Each agent can earn voting weight only by completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against hidden test cases and cross-validated by independently selected agents. A new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one stake across many accounts does not multiply influence; each account must separately spend time and resources to build a reliable record. An attacker may wander from harbor to harbor like a sparrow, but every fake account still pays the verification and task-completion cost before it can shape decisions.
